hypotheses.observation: The policy check evaluates error_rate_ratio with observed numerator 2 and denominator 100, operator 'lte', against threshold 0.01, and returns status FAIL; the finding list records this as a policy_failure for rule_id 'error-limit'.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The recorded 2 error samples out of 100 exceeded the configured 1% limit, which is the stated basis for the FAIL verdict. This is the direct metric-to-threshold comparison; it does not explain why the 2 errors occurred.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Reproduce the observed 2/100 from the source run and inspect the two error records (response codes, failure messages, request identifiers) to confirm they are genuine application failures rather than measurement artifacts.

hypotheses.possible_explanation: The two errors may both belong to the checkout sampler, or the overall run may consist only of the checkout sampler; per-sampler attribution is not shown, so either interpretation is possible but unproven.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare the underlying sample identifiers or per-sampler error logs to attribute each of the 2 errors to a specific sampler and to verify whether the overall and checkout sample sets are identical.

hypotheses.observation: Both metric summaries report latency p50=50, p95=95, p99=99, max=100 (ms), but no evidence links the 2 error records to those latency values.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The 2 errors could be concentrated near the observed tail (max latency 100 ms and p99 99 ms), but per-error latency is not provided, so the errors could carry any latency; this is only a hypothesis.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Assemble per-sample latency values, confirm whether error samples are included in or excluded from the reported percentiles, and check the latency of each of the 2 error records before drawing conclusions.

hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect the 2 error records' timestamps and any duration data, verify clock/timestamp consistency before inferring any temporal pattern, and compare with prior runs of the same test if such runs exist.

recommendations.action: Verify sampler attribution and time correctness: confirm which sampler(s) produced the 2 errors and check that clocks/timestamps used for any timing analysis are consistent before treating the errors as a checkout problem.
